A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerLA study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-E. The material supports reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, computational measurements, and supplementary training-strategy and embodied-task results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments removing GCN and varying Q-Former query-token counts.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported neighbor-search procedure: v1 matches through Hilbert indices, while v2 adds geometric partition labels and label-separated indexing before matching. This revises one component; the encoders, cross-attention, GCN, and consensus-loss architecture remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScanQA, ScanRefer, Nr3D, and the ScanNet portion of 3D-LLM. Scene description, embodied dialogue, and embodied planning were already evaluated in v1's appendix. The new ablations retain existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds the GCN-free PerLA variant as an evaluated comparator alongside the retained LL3DA†, Global, Local, and full PerLA rows. External baseline membership in the benchmark comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces a ScanQA experiment training LL3DA and PerLA from scratch with 32, 64, 96, and 128 query tokens, incorporating mirror-descent regularization after training divergence. Table 3 adds a GCN-removal control. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a GCN-removal ablation across three benchmarks and a query-token sensitivity study in Table J. The latter varies Q-Former queries directly, unlike the retained LL3DA† experiment combining local and global tokens. These are focused extensions to the existing ablation analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds a ScanQA CIDEr score of 77.61 without GCN, versus the retained 78.13 for full PerLA. New higher-token results include 128-token CIDEr scores of 77.0 for PerLA and 74.6 for LL3DA; v2 also reports divergence before regularization. Existing benchmark values remain unchanged, and Table J's 32-token PerLA row rounds an earlier from-scratch result.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces the index definition combined = label_offset × label + d, requiring the offset to exceed the maximum Hilbert distance to separate label ranges. Existing losses, complexity analysis, and Algorithms 1-2 remain unchanged. The added LL3DA† equation restates its previously described token construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and performance claims: preserving local and global information, Hilbert-based aggregation, GCN refinement, and consensus learning. The headline benchmark gains are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds geometric-consistency reasoning and asserts that label-constrained neighbors share an instance. It interprets the new ablations as supporting GCN and showing token-performance saturation around 96-128 queries. The limitations paragraph removes the explicit reference to outdoor generalization while retaining the broader complex-scenario limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds label-center computation, the label_offset condition, and per-batch sorting details. Appendix E.1 makes LL3DA†'s 64-by-768 token construction explicit. The new token study names its additional regularization but provides no detailed formulation or hyperparameters; existing hardware, budgets, and project access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds four cited works concerning an embodied generalist agent, superpoint graphs, Idefics2, and divergence-augmented policy optimization. It also connects the token-efficiency discussion to Idefics2. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording and spelling corrections, expands the neighbor-search and token-analysis explanations, adds acknowledgements, and adjusts author/contact presentation. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a row and revised caption, and a new appendix Table J displays the token sweep. Existing Tables J/K become K/L, and Figure F moves from PDF page 17 to 18. Other changes are spacing and reflow; retained figures show the same examples.

improvement.justification: The GCN-removal and direct query-token experiments provide useful additional evidence for existing design choices, while the geometric indexing description makes the procedure easier to inspect. These are limited gains because the main benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the newly introduced token-study regularization remains insufficiently specified for full reproduction.
